description: The 3D CAD branch tokens. Lengths are millimeters, angles degrees. Defaults describe a plain, conventional part (assumption values, not house values); the shipped hazard-protocol theme sets the house look and carries a note for each number. A floor or ceiling is a formula over the resolved DFM profile's paths: the token keeps its value, the effective value is the bound, and the resolved style says why.

classes.process: Preferences bounded by what the manufacturing process can make. Each may carry a floor or ceiling over DFM profile paths; with a resolved DFM profile the resolver reports the effective value and the reason, without one it reports the token as not checked against a process.
classes.structural: Values that carry load or keep a part honest about load. Never changed for looks: a restyle refuses them, and a structural claim needs an analysis or a test, not a preference.
classes.layout: Alignment, margins, datums and split placement. Changed only when the user asks, because moving features changes fits and mates.
classes.cosmetic: How the part looks. Free to change.

tokens.title: Form language
tokens.description: The edge vocabulary of the whole product. chamferRoundedCorners: chamfers where faces meet, rounded corners in plan view (angular but smooth); fillet: soft rounds on outer edges; chamfer: chamfers everywhere; sharp: no treatment.
tokens.guard: With chamferRoundedCorners the chamfer must be smaller than the plan-view corner radius it sweeps around, or the chamfer self-intersects at the corner (the agent checks it on each body).

tokens.title: Top and side edge treatment
tokens.description: Treatment of the edges where an upward-facing or side face meets another face (the edge loop around the top of a body).

tokens.title: Plan-view corner treatment
tokens.description: Treatment of the vertical edges, the corners of the body seen from above. Rounds here print in the XY plane as a smooth toolpath.

tokens.title: Chamfer angle
tokens.description: Angle of every chamfer on upper and side edges, measured from the face it cuts (45 is symmetric). One angle per product.

tokens.title: Chamfer ladder
tokens.description: The few chamfer sizes a product uses, smallest first. Every chamfer is one of them.
tokens.guard: Each size at least one line width and two layers, or the chamfer does not show as a face.

tokens.title: Bed edge chamfer
tokens.description: Chamfer on the edges that sit on the build plate. Bed edges are chamfered, never filleted: a bottom fillet is an overhang, a bottom chamfer prints cleanly and hides first-layer squish.
tokens.guard: At least the process's bed-edge chamfer.

tokens.title: Bed edge chamfer angle
tokens.description: Angle of the bed edge chamfer face from the build plate.
tokens.guard: The chamfer face is a downward-facing overhang: its angle from the plate is at least 90 degrees minus the process's maximum overhang angle (measured from vertical).

tokens.title: Edge break
tokens.description: The small edge break on secondary details (bosses, tabs, port openings) that are not part of the main edge vocabulary.
tokens.guard: At least half a line width and one layer, or it does not print as a feature.

tokens.title: Plan-view radius family
tokens.description: The small family of plan-view corner radii a product uses, smallest first, chosen by eye. Every plan-view corner is one of them.
tokens.guard: Each radius at least one line width, or the corner prints sharp and does not read as rounded.

tokens.title: Inside corner radius
tokens.description: Fillet on inside (concave) corners that do not carry load: pocket corners, recess corners.
tokens.guard: At least half a line width: the nozzle cannot turn a tighter inside corner, so a smaller value is not what prints.

tokens.title: Nested corner rule
tokens.description: outerMinusOffset: a feature inset from a rounded outline at a constant offset (a lid, a recess, a bezel) has corner radius equal to the outer radius minus the offset, so the gap reads as constant; when that falls below the smallest radius in the family, use the smallest.

tokens.title: Breaking the vocabulary
tokens.description: functionalOnly: an edge leaves the form language only to signal function (a touch point, a release, a warning, a mating face), never because another edge was easier to model.

tokens.title: Curvature continuity
tokens.description: g1: tangent blends everywhere; g2ShowFaces: curvature-continuous blends on large show faces that will be painted or polished. On as-printed parts layer lines hide the difference on small radii.

tokens.title: Proportion aid
tokens.description: An optional diagnostic aid for checking overall block proportions. Never a generator of dimensions; none means no proportion system is used or reported.

tokens.title: Margin
tokens.description: Offset from a face edge (or from the nearest secondary form) to every hole, vent, label, button and pattern zone on that face. One margin per face family.
tokens.guard: Changed only when asked; a margin smaller than the wall around a hole is a structural question for dfm.

tokens.title: Gutter
tokens.description: Spacing between related features inside a group (a light and its label, a row of ports); unrelated groups sit farther apart than this.
tokens.guard: Changed only when asked.

tokens.title: Near-miss distance
tokens.description: Feature edges or centerlines closer than this to a datum or to each other, but not on it, are near misses to snap together.
tokens.guard: Reported by the self-check; snapping happens only when the user asks.

tokens.title: Symmetry
tokens.description: mirrorPrimary: the primary form is mirror-symmetric about its main axis; asymmetric features (ports, switches) form one deliberate group on one side.
tokens.guard: Changed only when asked.

tokens.title: Shared datums
tokens.description: The named lines feature edges and centerlines land on (centerlines, the inner wall line, the board's baseline, a port baseline).
tokens.guard: Changed only when asked.

tokens.title: Heights on layer multiples
tokens.description: Horizontal steps, grooves, chamfer starts and color-change heights land on multiples of the layer height, so their edges print crisp.
tokens.guard: Uses layer.height from the DFM profile; without one the agent leaves heights as modeled.

tokens.title: Split placement
tokens.description: existingEdge: a split between two parts sits on an existing edge or change of direction, never mid-face, with each half printable without support.
tokens.guard: Changed only when asked; moving a split changes the parts.

tokens.title: Split style
tokens.description: shadowLine: one half laps over the other so the seam reads as a deliberate dark line and the halves self-locate; reveal: an intentional gap; recessedLid: a flat lid sunk in a recess; butt: faces meet.

tokens.title: Reveal width
tokens.description: Visible width of the shadow line or reveal at a split.
tokens.guard: At least the process's smallest printable gap.

tokens.title: Reveal depth
tokens.description: Depth of the shadow line or reveal groove.
tokens.guard: At least one line width, or the groove does not read as a shadow.

tokens.title: Seam placement
tokens.description: Where the slicer's layer-start seam goes on a cosmetic part; recorded in the part's metadata for the slicer step.

tokens.title: Show face
tokens.description: Which face is the show face. decidePerPart: the agent names the show face of each part and orients it (top surface, textured plate, or vertical wall), and records it.

tokens.title: Visible fasteners
tokens.description: How fasteners on show faces appear: hidden (under feet or labels, on the bottom), recessed (counterbored to one depth), flush (countersunk), exposed.

tokens.title: Fastener head
tokens.description: The head style of visible fasteners; one style per product.

tokens.title: Fastener kinds
tokens.description: Most distinct fastener types and sizes in one product; each extra kind needs a reason.

tokens.title: Text face
tokens.description: The face of embossed or engraved text; a bold sans-serif prints best. Usually a reference to a core typography token.

tokens.title: Text case
tokens.description: Case of text on parts.

tokens.title: Text style
tokens.description: emboss: raised; engrave: cut in; inlay: a color change on the first layers of the bed face.

tokens.title: Smallest cap height
tokens.description: The smallest cap height the style uses for text on parts, sized by cap height, not by the text box.
tokens.guard: At least the process's smallest legible text height.

tokens.title: Smallest stroke
tokens.description: The thinnest stroke of text and icons on parts.
tokens.guard: At least the process's smallest text stroke.

tokens.title: Emboss height
tokens.description: Height of raised text and marks.
tokens.guard: At least the process's emboss height.

tokens.title: Engrave depth
tokens.description: Depth of engraved text and marks.
tokens.guard: At least the process's engrave depth; never deeper than leaves the process's minimum wall behind it (checked by the agent against the wall).

tokens.title: Logo on parts
tokens.description: The logo asset embossed or engraved on parts; usually a reference to the core logo, gated by core brand.mode.

tokens.title: Mark placement
tokens.description: Where a mark goes: on a secondary face or in a dedicated recess, aligned to a datum, never floating on the show face.

tokens.title: Mark height
tokens.description: Height of a logo or mark on a part.
tokens.guard: At least twice the process's smallest text height, because a mark's finest feature is a fraction of its height.

tokens.title: Mark clear space
tokens.description: Clear zone around a mark on a part, as a share of the mark's height.

tokens.title: Signature pattern
tokens.description: The pattern used when a part gets one: lightening, stiffening or flair in a bounded zone. none: no pattern unless asked.

tokens.title: Pattern zone border
tokens.description: Solid band around every pattern zone, merged into the edges and bosses around it; also at least twice the rib or strut width (checked by the agent).
tokens.guard: At least the process's structural wall, so the zone edge is a wall and not a sliver.

tokens.title: Pocket ceiling span
tokens.description: Longest horizontal ceiling a pattern may leave on a vertical wall (a flat-top hex, an apex-down isogrid pocket); a longer pocket gets a pointed top or turns so its ceiling slopes.
tokens.guard: At most the process's longest bridge.

tokens.title: Blind pattern depth
tokens.description: Depth of a pattern recessed into a skin as texture rather than cut through.
tokens.guard: At least two layers, or the pattern does not read.

tokens.title: Structural claim
tokens.description: roleStated: the part note names the wall the pattern replaces and its role from the patterns reference (stiffens a thinner wall, carries local loads, or styling against a same-depth closed wall), with no load rating; analyzed: a load rating, set only with a calculation, simulation or coupon test linked.
tokens.guard: Never changed for looks; analyzed needs evidence (a calculation, a simulation or a coupon test).

tokens.title: Isogrid triangle height
tokens.description: Height h of each equilateral triangle cell (side a = 2h divided by the square root of 3).
tokens.guard: At least three cells across the panel's shortest span (the smeared stiffness formulas over-predict with fewer); checked by the agent.

tokens.title: Isogrid rib width
tokens.description: Rib (wall) width b; pick a width the slicer fills with whole perimeters.
tokens.guard: At least two line widths.

tokens.title: Isogrid rib depth
tokens.description: Rib depth d measured from the skin.
tokens.guard: Depth at most about five rib widths (a rib with a free top edge reaches local buckling near the material's strength around d = 5b, derived; thin deep ribs also wobble while printing; root fillets and nodes add margin). Shallow ribs still stiffen a thin skin (d = t gives about twice the skin's stiffness), but most of the gain comes with depth; checked by the agent.

tokens.title: Isogrid skin
tokens.description: Skin thickness t under a skinned isogrid.
tokens.guard: At least the process's minimum wall.

tokens.title: Isogrid backing
tokens.description: skinned: ribs on one side of a continuous skin (the skin is the show face and the seal); open: a through lattice for brackets loaded in plane and visible panels.
tokens.guard: An open lattice in a thin printed wall turns a shell into ribs bonded only at layer lines; dfm decides whether the part can take it.

tokens.title: Isogrid pocket corner rule
tokens.description: equalsRibWidth: each triangular pocket's corners are rounded with a radius equal to the rib width, capped at 0.4 times the pocket's inscribed radius; fixed: one radius from the radius family; none: sharp corners.

tokens.title: Isogrid node circles
tokens.description: Whether a boss with a hole sits where ribs meet. Machined isogrids have them because the cutter leaves material there; a printed one needs a boss only where something mounts.

tokens.title: Isogrid orientation
tokens.description: ribFamilyHorizontal: on vertical walls one rib family runs horizontal, so every pocket ceiling is either self-supporting or a short bridge.
tokens.guard: Pocket ceilings on vertical walls stay within pattern.pocket.ceiling.span.

tokens.title: Small pocket rule
tokens.description: dropUnderTwoRibWidths: a pocket whose inscribed radius is under two rib widths (cut short by a border, a boss or an edge) is left solid instead of filleted.

tokens.title: Voronoi strut width
tokens.description: Constant width of the walls between Voronoi cells (offset each cell inward by half of it).
tokens.guard: At least two line widths.

tokens.title: Voronoi cell size
tokens.description: Mean opening across a Voronoi cell; about five to ten strut widths reads well.
tokens.guard: At least 3 mm and six line widths: small openings close up when printed (derived, unverified).

tokens.title: Voronoi cell corner rule
tokens.description: equalsStrutWidth: every cell corner is rounded with a radius equal to the strut width; fixed: one radius from the radius family; none: sharp corners.

tokens.title: Voronoi relaxation
tokens.description: Centroid relaxation passes on the seeds: 0 is raw random cells, a few passes give even but organic cells, many converge toward hexagons.

tokens.title: Hex cell size
tokens.description: Across-flats size of each hexagonal opening.
tokens.guard: At least 3 mm and six line widths (derived, unverified).

tokens.title: Hex wall width
tokens.description: Wall width between hexagonal openings.
tokens.guard: At least two line widths.

tokens.title: Wall preference
tokens.description: The wall thickness the style prefers for load-bearing walls. Style may thicken a wall, never thin it below what the process and the loads need.
tokens.guard: Never changed for looks; at least the process's structural wall.

tokens.title: Load root fillet
tokens.description: Fillet where load-bearing walls, ribs and bosses meet a base (about half a rib width under an isogrid rib).
tokens.guard: Never reduced for looks; at least half a line width.

tokens.title: Keep load paths
tokens.description: A restyle never removes or thins a rib, gusset, boss or wall that carries load; a pattern zone never cuts through one.
tokens.guard: Never changed for looks.

tokens.title: Body color
tokens.description: Color of the primary parts (the filament or finish color named by its role).

tokens.title: Secondary color
tokens.description: Color of supporting and structural parts.

tokens.title: Accent color
tokens.description: Accent parts and details; a color change sits at a geometric break (a step, a groove, a chamfer start), never mid-face.

tokens.title: Surface finish
tokens.description: The surface look asked of the material and the print: matte hides layer lines, silk and gloss show them.

tokens.title: Material look preference
tokens.description: A preference for how the material looks. The material itself is chosen for loads, heat and environment by the process skill; style never overrides that choice.
tokens.guard: A preference only: dfm-3d-printing chooses the material.

tokens.title: Default process
tokens.description: The manufacturing process the style assumes when a part says nothing else; the DFM profile the resolver checks against should be for this process.
tokens.guard: The process of a real part is chosen with dfm; this is only the assumption a new part starts from.
